change.description: Span Buffer Multiprocess Enhancement with Health Monitoring
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: Unhealthy flusher processes are no longer killed before a replacement starts
findings.body: The old code called `self.process.kill()` unconditionally. The new code only kills when `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`. Processes come from `self.mp_context.Process` with the spawn context (line 105), so they are `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess`. That class subclasses `process.BaseProcess`, not `multiprocessing.Process` (`context.Process`), so the check is always False and `kill()` is never called. When a process is detected as `hang`, line 259 starts a second process for the same shards while the hung one keeps running. If the hung one recovers (for example a stalled Redis or Kafka call returns), both flush the same queues at once, which can produce duplicate or fragmented segments. Each hang leaks another process, up to MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS. Fix: go back to calling `process.kill()` with the `ValueError` guard, and skip it only for `threading.Thread`, e.g. `if not isinstance(process, threading.Thread)` or `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess)`. The same wrong check in `join` (line 346) means `terminate()` never runs there either. That one predates this PR.

findings.title: join() skips terminate for the remaining processes once the deadline passes
findings.body: Once the deadline has passed, `break` exits the loop before `process.terminate()` runs for the current process and every process after it. The old code always reached the terminate step after the wait. With several processes and a timeout, the first process's wait can use up the whole deadline, so the others are left running after `join` returns. They are daemons, so they only die when the parent exits. On a rebalance, though, a new flusher is created while these keep flushing their shards. Fix: replace `break` with skipping only the wait, and always try to terminate each remaining process (and fix the isinstance check noted at line 254 so terminate actually runs).

findings.title: `spans.buffer.max-flush-segments` now caps each process, not the consumer
findings.body: Each process gets its own `SpansBuffer(shards)`. `flush_segments` computes `max_segments_per_shard = ceil(max_flush_segments / len(self.assigned_shards))` from that buffer's own shards (src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:382-384). The total flushed per cycle is therefore up to `num_processes × max-flush-segments`, where it used to be `max-flush-segments`. Kafka/Redis load grows when operators raise `--flusher-processes`. If this is intended, document the new meaning; if not, divide the option by `num_processes`.

findings.title: Redis memory info is fetched once per process buffer, but each call covers the whole cluster
findings.body: `get_memory_info` returns `iter_cluster_memory_usage(self.client)` for the whole cluster, whatever the shards (src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:375-376). Looping over `self.buffers` runs the same cluster-wide INFO query N times per `submit` and counts every node N times. The ratio stays correct because `used` and `available` are both multiplied by N, but the work is wasted. Calling it once, on any one buffer, is enough.

findings.title: `time.sleep(0.1)` is a no-op here because the test monkeypatches `time.sleep`
findings.body: Line 15 does `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)`, so `time.sleep(0.1)` returns immediately. The comment says it gives the flusher threads time to process. It doesn't, so `step.join()` still sets `stopped` right after the drift change. A thread that hasn't yet looped with the new drift exits without flushing, and `(msg,) = messages` fails intermittently. Either keep a reference to the real sleep before monkeypatching, or poll until `messages` is non-empty, with a timeout, before calling `join`.

findings.title: `_create_process_for_shard` is never called
findings.body: Nothing calls `_create_process_for_shard`. Restarts go through `_create_process_for_shards` directly (line 259). Remove it.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag key: `shards` here, `shard` elsewhere
findings.body: `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` is tagged `shards`, while `flusher.produce` and `segment_size_bytes` (lines 185, 195) use `shard` for the same comma-joined value. Using one key makes dashboards consistent.

findings.title: Docstring says one process per shard; the CLI default is one process total
findings.body: The `--flusher-processes` CLI default is 1 (src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py:434). Shards are spread round-robin over `min(max_processes, len(shards))` processes (lines 60-66). Only a `None`/0 value from code paths that skip the CLI gives one process per shard. Reword it, e.g. 'Distributes shards across up to `max_processes` processes.'

contracts.action: Restart an unhealthy flusher process (dead or hung)
contracts.before_after: Before: kill always attempted (ValueError ignored). After: kill gated on isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process), which is False for SpawnProcess, so a hung process survives and a duplicate is started for the same shards.
contracts.visible_effect: Possible duplicate/concurrent flushing of the same Redis shard queues into buffered-segments; leaked processes.
contracts.failure_mode: Hung process never killed; after MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS the consumer raises RuntimeError.

contracts.action: Wait for all flusher processes on join(timeout)
contracts.equivalent_path: Previous single-process join loop followed by terminate
contracts.before_after: Overall wait is bounded by the deadline across all processes (shared deadline). But after the deadline, the loop breaks without terminating the remaining processes.
contracts.visible_effect: Remaining flusher processes keep running after join returns (until parent exit, since they are daemons).
contracts.failure_mode: With timeout=None, waits until each process observes stopped; a hung process blocks join forever (same as before).

contracts.action: Per-process SpansBuffer flushes its shard subset
contracts.equivalent_path: SpansBuffer.flush_segments with the full assigned_shards list
contracts.before_after: max-flush-segments was split across all shards; now it is split per buffer, so the total per cycle scales with the number of processes.
contracts.visible_effect: Higher flush throughput/load per cycle than the option suggests.

contracts.action: Aggregate Redis memory info across process buffers
contracts.before_after: Same cluster-wide query repeated N times; the ratio is unchanged.
contracts.visible_effect: None functionally; extra Redis INFO calls per submit.
contracts.failure_mode: A Redis error raises out of submit, as before.

contracts.action: New --flusher-processes CLI option passed to the factory and flusher
contracts.before_after: Default 1 means all shards are handled by one process (same as before); larger values spread shards round-robin.
contracts.visible_effect: Operators control the flusher process count.

summary: The PR splits the span flusher into several processes, each handling a subset of shards. One bug blocks the merge. A flusher process detected as hung or dead is no longer killed before its replacement starts. The new `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` check is always False for spawn-context processes, so a hung process keeps running next to the new one for the same shards. Separately, `join()` stops waiting at the deadline without terminating the remaining processes. In the tests, the added `time.sleep(0.1)` in test_basic does nothing because the test monkeypatches `time.sleep`, so the race it was meant to fix is still there. Smaller points: `max-flush-segments` now applies per process instead of per consumer, the cluster-wide memory query runs once per process, one method is never called, a metric tag key is inconsistent, and the class docstring is out of date.
